Astronomers have discovered a planet where the surface is a continuous ocean of magma. She is not like any known today. It is about the exoplanet L98-59d, located approximately 35 light years from Earth. It is 1.6 times larger than our planet and revolves around a small red star. At first, scientists assumed that there could be an ocean of water on it. But new research has shown otherwise: beneath the surface, there probably stretches a giant ocean of magma, thousands of kilometers long, that may even include a molten core. The temperature on the surface can reach about 1,900°C, and the atmosphere probably contains a lot of hydrogen sulfide, a gas with the smell of rotten eggs. Researchers believe that this discovery may indicate the existence of a whole new class of planets. Such worlds may be much more common than previously thought, prompting scientists to reassess which exoplanets might be habitable.

Every time they talk about agricultural reform, the story repeats itself: the agricultural lobby warns of a collapse, claims that the problem is not theirs at all, and promises that imports will not lower prices for the consumer. There is no competition, no entry of new players, and almost no imports - because of suffocating tariffs. And the result? High prices for the consumer, without direct connection to production efficiency. Even the "target price", which sounds neutral, is structured so that it is strongly influenced by small and expensive dairy farms - some of which do not participate in the cost survey at all. The proposed reform does not "eliminate agriculture", but changes the rules of the game: instead of closed quotas - protected liters at a lower price, opening the market, and creating an incentive for inefficient dairy farms to retire with compensation. And at the same time - a real possibility for importing and introducing new manufacturers. And those who claim that imports "do not pass on to the consumer" - should look at the fish market after the removal of tariffs in 2016 and 2022, frozen fish prices fell by 8.3%, while other food products jumped by more than 22%. The question now is: does the state manage a closed market for the benefit of an organized group, or does it open it to competition so that a basic product like milk is sold at a fair price? The phenomenon of original antigenic sin (OAS) has been described in relation to SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19 inoculations and has the potential to lead to Antibody Dependent Enhancement (ADE). In this scenario, the antibodies that the vaccine generated actually help the virus infect greater numbers of cells than it would have on its own. In this situation, the antibodies bind to the virus and help it more easily get into cells than it would on its own. The result is often more severe illness than if the person had been unvaccinated. Because of the continued antigenic evolution of viruses, they accumulate mutations in the antibody epitopes and proteins that allow them to escape from immunity generated by prior vaccination or infection, a process known as “antigenic drift.” Antigenic drift occurs in unpredictable stops and starts, and at different rates for different types and subtypes of the virus. The mechanisms that might be responsible for a negative effect of prior vaccination on vaccine effectiveness are not fully understood, but the finding that the magnitude of the negative effect depends on antigenic distance could be consistent with antigenic focusing. In this case, when sequentially exposed to (2) antigenically related viruses, the immune system focuses on the shared epitopes at the expense of novel epitopes on the second virus that might be important for the protection against a third, antigenically drifted virus. In contrast, a person who has not been previously vaccinated might mount a broader response against all of the epitopes in the vaccine. Other potential mechanisms could include interference by prior immunity on antigenic presentation, or the “infection-block hypothesis.” In this case, prior vaccination reduces prior infections with the virus, which in turn would have provided more effective protection against subsequent drifted infection than the vaccine does, resulting in lower rates of illness in subjects with infection-based immunity than in those with vaccine-induced immunity.

A role for selenium-dependent GPX1 in SARS-CoV-2 virulence "Among the proteins most impacted by selenium status is glutathione peroxidase 1 (GPX1), a cytosolic selenoenzyme with known antiviral properties. Viral infection increases reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in host cells, which, if not counterbalanced by antioxidant defense mechanisms, leads to oxidative stress. Excess oxidative stress, in turn, augments mutation of the viral genome, which can lead to the emergence of more virulent strains. GPX1 comprises a key defense against ROS, catalyzing the detoxification of hydrogen peroxide to water. In mice lacking the Gpx1 gene (Gpx1−/−), inoculation of a benign strain of coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3) led to viral genome mutations, increased virulence, and myocarditis, none of which were observed in wild-type mice. Moreover, the Gpx1−/− model recapitulated the effect of a selenium-deficient diet in wild-type mice, promoting mutagenesis of the benign CVB3 strain into a virulent one. In addition, both selenium-deficient wild-type mice (6) and Gpx1−/− mice exhibit heightened inflammatory responses and more severe lung pathology in response to inoculation with influenza A, further indicating that GPX1 participates in molecular mechanisms protecting against viral infections of the respiratory tract. It is currently unknown whether SARS-CoV-2 is also modulated by GPX1 activity, but recent findings are highly suggestive."

📝Telegram is trying to survive📝 In recent days, against the backdrop of Telegram blocking, complaints about the inaccessibility of other Russian resources, which no one seems to have blocked, have become more frequent. Conversely, access to prohibited social networks periodically returns. Apparently, the fact is that the system of technical means for countering threats (TSPU) cannot cope with the load, and blocked resources again began to “leak” to users. 🔻What happened and why? ▪️TSPU are filters through which all Internet traffic of Russian operators physically passes. The principle is simple: everything incoming is analyzed, “undesirable” is cut off. It works as long as there is not too much traffic. ▪️The problem arose not because of the blocking of Telegram as such, but because of MTProxy, the messenger’s built-in proxy protocol. Millions of Russian users, not wanting to lose access, switched en masse to public MTProxy servers. These servers generate a huge flow of “junk” traffic, which is disguised as regular HTTPS and which TSPUs are obliged to analyze. Public nodes die under load every few hours, after which users look for new ones - and the cycle repeats. ▪️The total throughput of all TSPUs in Russia is estimated at approximately 132 Tbit/s. With today's load, this is no longer enough: nodes periodically go into bypass mode - and at these moments traffic passes through without filtering. It was then that WhatsApp, Instagram and other extremist services banned in the Russian Federation began to work “on their own” among Russians. 📌The scale of MTProxy use and TSPU overload indicate one thing: despite all the inconveniences and risks, Russian users do not want to leave Telegram. This is because over the years, the messenger has already become an important social and information infrastructure: there are family chats, work groups, news channels based on interests, and local communities. Therefore, attempts by individual LOMs to promote themselves during blocking only generate public negativity - Deputy Svintsov is a witness to this. And the desire to forcibly tear users away from an already working tool in any case causes antagonism, even if an alternative is offered. And there is still a lot of work to be done on MAX so that users find the platform convenient and safe for organizing work and personal affairs there. Radicals and cytokines are intimately involved in the genesis of the endothelial damage, which is the common denominator of multi-organ failure in COVID-19. When ARDS occurs, ROS, RNS and cytokine production is out of control, and attempting to contrast all with a single cytokine inhibitor is doomed to fail. Only one drug is capable of inhibiting the production of all three of these classes of substance: methylene blue. Methylene blue inhibits the formation of superoxide anion (ROS precursor) by blocking the xanthine oxidase pathway; it counteracts the synthesis of nitric oxide (RNS precursor) by direct inhibition of NO-synthase, and inhibits cytokine expression via attenuation of NF-kB signaling. Methylene blue is a tricyclic phenothiazine, approved by the FDA and EMA for the treatment of methaemoglobinaemia and malaria. It is also used to inactivate viruses in blood products for transfusion, in the presence of UV light. Recent (non peer-reviewed) in vitro studies indicate that it has antiviral activity in the absence of UV light, strengthening the rationale for its use in COVID-19. However, methylene blue use in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is contraindicated due to increased risk of haemolytic anemia. Its concomitant use with serotonin reuptake inhibitors is also contraindicated. Methylene blue is a potent reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase A (the enzyme that catalyses serotonin breakdown) and concomitant use with serotonin reuptake inhibitors can inhibit the degradation of serotonin and increase its concentration to toxic levels (serotonin syndrome).

The organization developed a multidisciplinary professional doctrine in the field of "health of abductees and families of abductees", published reports and articles and made accessible the health, medical and mental implications of abduction to decision makers in Israel and around the world, with an emphasis on humanitarian and international organizations. At the same time, a unique professional and public language was formulated to understand the multidimensional damage of the kidnapping and to sharpen the sense of urgency to return all the abductees, alive and dead. The organization regularly accompanied the families, initiated collaborations with the health system and treatment providers, motivated the health and scientific community in Israel and the world, and took part in professional initiatives, conferences and public activities. In addition to this, he identified and mapped the unique needs of the families of the abductees and the survivors of the captivity, worked for professional advocacy and the exploitation of rights, and accompanied rehabilitation and long-term support, while laying the foundation for future research on the effects of the abduction on the health of the families and the returnees. The resilience team was established immediately with the establishment of the headquarters, when about ten women and therapists were stationed to help. First the resilience team members joined all the intense protest activities, marches, rallies, demonstrations, and provided emotional support as needed. The caregivers were in close contact with most of the families and their door was open to help anyone who needed it at any hour of the day. As the struggle dragged on and the headquarters was organized, mental support gradually became structured: a clinic was opened for urgent and short interventions and diagnosis. The clinic has created a significant therapeutic sequence with external therapists for long-term treatments. In addition, the headquarters teams who worked closely with the families with a huge emotional investment, and especially the family teams, the media teams, the family room team and the field headquarters, received a therapist who joined the teams for counseling, training, and individual help. As the struggle continued and its consequences on the mental state of the family members, diverse activities were added: group therapy for homogeneous groups, such as families of martyrs, mothers of abductees, young people, etc.; days of respite; Retreats for homogenous groups with two-three days of therapeutic activity and consolidation and relaxation activities. Oil Minister Hayan Abdel-Ghani said production at the Basra Oil Company had been cut to 900,000 barrels per day from 3.3 million. The produced oil is being redirected to keep refineries operating. The scale of the reduction will be reviewed depending on developments in the region, and companies have been invited to urgent negotiations on operations, costs, and staffing under force majeure conditions. From the article: Superficiality, negligence and lack of motivation - this is the picture reflected from a review of the investigation file against "Brothers in Arms" activists who participated in the attack on the offices of the Ecclesiastical Forum about three years ago. The review of the file, which came to us about two and a half months after we reported here on the intention to close it, as indeed happened, raises serious questions about the manner in which the investigation was conducted, and whether whoever conducted it was even interested in reaching results. As you may recall, in March 2023 the activists of "Brothers in Arms", an organization that was still relatively unknown at the time, launched the new organization in a well-publicized "occupation" operation of the entrance to the offices of the Ecclesiastical Forum on Am Walom Street in Jerusalem. What raised the anger of members of the Brothers in Arms was the right-wing approach and nationalistic conception of the research institute, the position papers it produced, among other things, for Knesset members from the right wing of the map, and especially its firm support for legal reform. The action at the Forum's offices was one link in a long chain of protest actions directed in those days against the congregation, its activists, and also against the philanthropists who financially supported its activities (a protest that largely achieved its goal, after a major donor stopped his financial support for the organization). The reports from that morning and the testimonies of those who were lucky enough to be in the offices that morning, paint a picture of a violent attack on the offices of a civil society organization. An employee who was in the office that morning described threats directed at him, and the CEO of the Forum, who was called to the scene, experienced a violent attack. N., a young employee of the Forum who arrived at work early that morning, was locked in the offices and could not leave them for a long time. The participants in the violent attack did not hide, although some wore masks. The photos of the vandalism of the entrance to the Forum's offices, the placement of sandbags and the deployment of a barbed wire fence were distributed in the media. Some of the participants They even took pride in participating in the event and willingly associated themselves with acts that constitute criminal offenses, including trespassing, trespassing, and even false imprisonment. In July, the lawyers of the Forum and N. were informed that the investigation case against all those involved was closed, and that no indictment would be filed And according to the response given to this article, it seems that there is not enough evidence for prosecution. When you compare the indictment filed against Shafi Paz and Doron Abrahami, who sprayed graffiti in Tel Aviv, the failure in handling the incident by the police and the prosecutor's office is doubly obvious. The investigation file includes 110 documents The transcripts of the interrogations of the seven detainees on the day of the incident, as well as two testimonies of those who were present at the offices at the time - one was taken at the offices, and the other at the police station. In the second testimony it is explicitly stated that the speaker is Alan Batofin, who was the head of the house at the office, while the name of the person who gave the testimony was deleted from the copy of the file, but it seems that he also gave it in Tafoin. In addition, the file contains many technical documents such as delay reports, documents Release on bail and the like, as well as the action reports of the police officers who were called to the incident. A police team was also called to the scene and collected findings and took fingerprints from signs hung on the spot and adhesive papers. Two other important documents are a message given by the CEO of the Kehalat Forum, Meir Rubin, in which he complained about his attack and identified Itai Brandes, who he says was one of the participants in the attack, as well as the transcript of Brandes' investigation. Specialists of the reconnaissance and observation squadron of the 30th Commando Regiment of the UK, including a group from the 148th battery, disembarked from a German submarine S185 (Type-212A). The operation was carried out in a covert mode: the personnel with their equipment boarded the submarine using inflatable boats, after which the submarine submerged. And it would be good to understand what the citizens of the republic ultimately voted for. 📌According to the authorities, the adopted constitution creates a new balance of checks and balances in the state, and also opens equal access to parliament for any political parties. Formally, this is true, but not for the president, who is turning into an uncontrollable arbiter. 🔻People's Parliament ➡️On the one hand, in Kazakhstan, instead of a bicameral parliament, a unicameral “Kurultai” appears, in which there will be no presidential quota, and all deputies will be based on party lists. In Astana this was explained by the desire to strengthen the voice of the people. ➡️On the other hand, although the Kurultai will officially be given the right to approve presidential candidates for government positions, a double refusal will allow Tokayev to dissolve such a parliament. What kind of motivation will the deputies have in this case to go “against the grain” is obvious. ➡️Of course, for any controversial issues there is a decision of the Constitutional Court, but within the framework of the new constitution, the Kurultai will be able to deprive its judges of immunity, as well as the judges of the Supreme Court, which the latter will keep in mind. 🔻What are the risks? ➡️But even such a system is not immune from failures. And here another new body comes onto the scene - the People's Council with the “right of legislative initiative.” Unlike parliament, where the president's influence is formally limited, a council of a chairman and 126 members will be appointed by Tokayev. ➡️If the political system is still under threat, the vertical of power will strengthen the position of the vice president. As planned, such a structure itself will complicate attempts at any constitutional coup. The experience of January 2022 affected this. ❗️With all this, the main question remains the possible “reset” of Tokayev’s term. The head of Kazakhstan himself denies this possibility, declaring that he will only serve until 2029. However, if he still changes his mind, only one decision of a loyal Constitutional Court is enough.
